relevance_note: Case report of a LAMP2 variant carrier with Danon disease and his family: "Genetic testing identified a hemizygous LAMP2 mutation (c.865-2A>G, exon 7, NM_002294)".
method_note: Hand extraction; JSON assembled by a short script in scratch. Proband labelled II-1 (the paper's own pedigree label, used once; elsewhere 'the patient'). Relatives labelled by rule 2: mother, father (tested negative), three daughters (numbered daughter of II-1, 2, 3 in no paper-given order) and one son. The abstract says 'Testing of his mother and 3 children also revealed the LAMP2 variant' and the timeline says the 3 daughters were diagnosed with Danon disease and the son was not, but the paper never says which 3 children carry the variant, so no variant rows were made for the children. Contradictions/notes: (1) ACMG criteria list PS2 (de novo) while the text says the mother carries the variant (heterozygous) and the father does not; inheritance recorded as inherited maternal per D-24. (2) 'skeletal muscle ... findings were normal' vs 'limb muscle strength was graded 4/5'; both feature rows emitted, checklist proximal muscle weakness left not reported (weakness also not stated as proximal). Figure 4 legend describes muscle fibers/type I fibers while the text says cardiomyocytes; only the text finding was recorded. (3) 'Development ... normal' used to exclude developmental delay (D-27); 'intelligence ... normal' excluded intellectual disability as a feature but the composite checklist item (incl. learning difficulties) left not reported; 'retinal findings were normal' recorded as excluded retinal abnormality only, checklist pigmentary retinopathy left not reported (whole-exam rule). (4) Reduced ejection fraction checklist marked observed from Table 1 LVEF 18% (Jan 22, 2025) plus 'systolic' heart failure. (5) Age at diagnosis 18 years taken from the admission at 18 and genetic diagnosis on Day 17 of that admission. Age at death not stated (died 12 years after diagnosis), so deceased_age left null. Table 1 is a single-patient follow-up table; no stacked cells.
